newsitem.title: USA: Vermont Senate passes $757 million budget.
newsitem.headline: Vermont Senate passes $757 million budget.

text.p: The Vermont Senate gave final approval Friday to a $757 million state budget for fiscal year 1998 by a vote of 28-1.
Now the measure will have to be reconciled with the House-approved bill and there are significant differences.
The budget for fiscal year 1998 was approved 28-1. But it contains some significant differences from the House-approved budget including:
-- a $10 million increase in state aid to education,
-- an increase in money to protect farming and forestry land, known as Current Use.
-- $20 million for additional property tax relief.

Senator Jim Greenwood (R-Essex/Orleans) said that these increases were necessary to create a "bridge" to full property tax reform, set to take place in FY 1999. That property tax reform bill is still mired in debate in the Senate Finance Committee but is likely to be voted out next week.
A conference committee to reconcile the two measures is expected to be named next week.
